newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU sees no early move on S. Africa ostrich ban.
newsitem.headline: EU sees no early move on S. Africa ostrich ban.

text.p: The European Union is unlikely to move quickly to lift its ban on imports of South African ostrich meat despite hopes being raised by exporters, EU officials said on Thursday.
"The (EU's) scientific and veterinary committee will discuss the ban next week but will not have all the information they need to reach a decision," one official said.

The chairman of the South African National Ostrich Processors Association, Peter Strydom, said on Wednesday that research on whether the meat is safe for human consumption should be completed by Saturday.

The Commission said on November 14 it had banned EU member states from importing South African ostrich meat after an outbreak of Congo-Crimean haemorrhagic fever at South Africa's biggest abattoir last month.
Strydom said in an interview that he hoped that the findings of South African scientists, being examined by EU veterinary experts, would allow shipments to resume by next Wednesday.
EU veterinary experts are due to discuss the issue on Tuesday but will postpone a decision until a later meeting, the Commission official added.
